context.definition: The OHSS series count grants of U.S. permanent-resident status; the UN series count resident stocks. Neither is a measure of net migration. Grants include adjustments by people already in the United States, not only new physical arrivals. Birthplace is not a departure country.
context.periods: U.S. fiscal years end September 30, not December 31. Birthplace and nationality series remain separate.
context.resident_stocks: UN stocks refer to 1 July in actual published benchmark years. China destination estimates use foreign citizenship; Hong Kong and U.S. destination estimates use foreign birth. Refugee adjustments are included where flagged R. These are not new immigration or net migration. No annual observations are invented between benchmarks.
context.rights: Selected statistical aggregates and original figures only; no source workbooks are redistributed. UN estimates: United Nations DESA, Population Division, International Migrant Stock 2024, adapted under CC BY 3.0 IGO.
context.rounding: FY2015–2024 birthplace counts and FY2025 nationality counts are rounded to the nearest ten. Earlier figures use older, exact-count vintages.

coverage.description: China, Hong Kong and Macau birthplace series, FY2000–FY2024; all permanent-resident status grants.
China nationality category, FY2025 reported annual totals. Hong Kong and Macau are not separately identified in this table.
A comparable annual U.S.-to-mainland-China permanent-residency series has not been verified. All-foreigner visas, residence permits and border crossings are not substitutes.

UN bilateral resident estimates in both directions for mainland China and Hong Kong: 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2024. Mainland destination uses U.S. citizenship, not U.S. birthplace. These stocks are not immigration flows.
The reviewed UN bilateral table does not separately report the U.S.–Macau pair. No zero or allocation from mainland China is inferred.
